segments.text: Mezo gives anyone a Bitcoin-backed loan. Pylon lets you steer that loan: leverage it, deleverage it, or defend it — one transaction each, on the trove you already own.

Every Mezo trove sits in one redemption queue: four hundred and twenty-nine million MUSD deep across two hundred and ninety-six troves. Redemptions start at the lowest ratio above one hundred and ten percent, with no liquidation warning — and repaying needs MUSD a borrower may not have.
No wallet extension. Paste a key, and the terminal becomes that account — then size the loop: half a milli-BTC.
The x-ray prices every leg before anything is signed. Execute: the engine relays it, the signature authorises the change, and the position updates on chain. Confirmed on Mezo Testnet.

The shield reserve is the other half: one thousand one hundred and eight MUSD of pooled capital, lent only to a registered position, and only to repay its debt. The claim blocks collateral release until the loan is settled.

segments.text: Every operation resolves to a transaction: a flash loop, an unwind, a full exit, and a keeper defence that moved a position from one hundred and seventy-two back to one hundred and eighty-one percent. The same audited generation is live on mainnet.
One switch, two networks. The mainnet bundle reads Mezo directly — real contract addresses, real reserve state — while the testnet bundle keeps the hosted engine.
Pylon. Non-custodial leverage and defence for Mezo troves. Forty-three contract tests, a twelve-lens security review, a live terminal, and a public repository.

vars.tagline: A Bitcoin loan should be a position you can steer, not a contract you obey.
vars.headline:
Loop, unwind, exit, shield.
One transaction each — executed live.
